dataset.name: small, purpose-built fixture (56 products: 2 Sofas, 2 Boots, 1 Coffee Tables, 1 Bookshelves, plus 50 plain filler products; not a modification of the frozen generators)

repetitions: 5 independent full runs; benign-recovery/adversarial-false-recovery/NDCG numbers are deterministic byte-for-byte across all 5 (confirmed by direct diff, this fixture has zero RNG); latency is the median of 7 black_box-guarded batched trials per row per run, and still shows real run-to-run variance at this catalog's few-microsecond absolute scale -- both extremes of the 5-run range are reported below, not a single favorable run

headline_result.treatment_a: FAILS to recover any of the 4 preregistered benign rows (0/4): each compiles to a Hybrid outcome with a single ProductType structural constraint plus a one-word residual, and the delegate's own structural-set-restricted search for that residual word finds nothing (by fixture construction), so the query returns zero hits even though the entity alone has real, matching products. Confirms H2-A.
headline_result.treatment_b: recovers all 4 benign rows (mean NDCG@10 = 1.0000) but also recovers ALL THREE preregistered adversarial rows (3/3 false recovery, after the second-correction-round addition of row 9) -- 'banana' (observed nowhere), 'velvet' (observed only under a different product type), and 'velvet blue sofas' (a compound-constraint case) are all recovered exactly as readily as the genuinely uninformative benign words. Confirms H2-B. FAILS the GO gate. Latency overhead vs A: 3.3%-6.1% across 5 runs.
headline_result.treatment_c: behaves IDENTICALLY to B on every row of this workload, since the delegate's raw hits are empty for every structurally-anchored row here. Confirms H2-C. FAILS the GO gate. Latency overhead vs A: 4.4%-8.0% across 5 runs.
headline_result.treatment_d: recovers all 4 benign rows (mean NDCG@10 = 1.0000) AND correctly rejects all three adversarial rows (0/3 false recovery), with zero query-time model calls (structural fact). Confirms H2-D. PASSES every preregistered R2 GO-gate criterion -- but only after a second-correction-round fix (see below). Latency overhead vs A is real and substantially higher (46.8%-51.9% across 5 runs, up from the originally-published 36.6%-41.3% since row 9 adds one more Required-classified row to the same double-call pattern) with an identified, disclosed root cause specific to this experimental implementation (execute_d calls the real execute_planned a second time -- redundantly re-running the delegate search -- as its lazy 'stay at zero' fallback for Required-classified tokens; a production implementation with internal access to verify_and_truncate would not pay this cost twice) -- but R2's own preregistered GO gate has no latency threshold, unlike R1's, so this does not affect the verdict.
headline_result.verdict: GO for Treatment D. Unlike R1 (REVISE), R2 reaches a clean pass: Treatment D's compiled-residual-policy mechanism clears every preregistered GO-gate criterion (benign recovery, adversarial false recovery, zero query-time model calls). Per Issue #42's own rule, this is a real candidate for a RED-before-GREEN production change to commerce_core -- deliberately not made in this same pass; the production-change step itself is tracked separately (task #63, after R3), so R1/R2/R3's serving-contract decisions are reviewed together.
headline_result.reproducibility: all 5 runs byte-identical on every benign-recovery/adversarial-false-recovery/NDCG number (verified by direct diff excluding the latency_ms_per_call JSON block)
headline_result.fixture_design_note: Two problems found and fixed by direct source reading before any row was run: (1) compile_lexicon registers every Enum/MultiEnum value and true-Boolean attribute name unconditionally as a hard-constraint lexicon candidate -- every test residual word here is therefore a plain title word only, never a registered attribute value/name, or it could never remain residual text at all; (2) with only 6 real products, Sofas/Boots' 2-product share (33%) is far above the 0.05 selectivity threshold, so every row would have routed to Punt (whole-corpus delegate search, no restrict_to) instead of the intended Hybrid (delegate search restricted to the entity's own candidates, confirmed via direct read of phase9_eval::bitmap_delegate's BitmapRestrictQuery to filter inside the delegate's own scorer) -- silently replacing R2's intended test scenario with an unrelated one. Fixed by padding the fixture with 50 plain filler products until selectivity clears 0.05 with margin (2/56 ~= 3.6%), confirmed directly in this run's own compiled-query diagnostics (every structurally-anchored row shows outcome=Hybrid).
headline_result.second_correction_round: A fresh adversarial reviewer with no implementation task, before any production change was made on the strength of R2's GO verdict, independently recomputed every number/claim in this manifest from the raw artifacts and source (all confirmed) and found two real issues: (1) ResidualPolicy::classify treated 'observed anywhere under the query's own bare ProductTypeId' as a Preferred signal, independent of the query's actual (possibly narrower) structural candidate set -- R2's original 8-row workload only ever compiled a single ProductType constraint, so this was never exercised; reproduced directly (compile('velvet blue sofas', ...) compiles a compound ProductType(Sofas) AND Enum(color=Blue) constraint whose real candidate set is {P1} only, and pre-fix, Treatment D incorrectly recovered ProductId(1), a genuine false positive), then fixed by removing that condition entirely (cross-type breadth alone was already sufficient for every originally-published benign row, so the fix changes none of those numbers) and adding both a permanent regression test and the new adversarial row 9 to the GO-gate computation itself; (2) execute_c's only code path that distinguishes it from execute_b (the non-empty-raw reorder branch) had zero test coverage anywhere in this crate, closed with a dedicated unit test using a fixed-output stub delegate. Both independently reproduced before being fixed; neither reverses the GO verdict -- Treatment D still clears every gate criterion against the harder 9-row/3-adversarial-row workload. Full detail: docs/experiments/ISSUE42_LOG.md's 'Second correction round' section under I42-R2.
